answer: To secure an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks, networks can enforce a cryptographic proof-of-stake mechanism requiring each node to lock value behind a unique public key and associated cipher. Before embarking on any computational voyage, an agent must stake capital, rendering the creation of fake identities economically prohibitive. Furthermore, network reputation is permanently bound to this identity pigment, ensuring that malicious behavior immediately burns the attacker's staked capital and permanently invalidates their operational credentials.
